decisions.reason: As a decorative carpet close to the existing assortment, it fits the firm's material and interior-design knowledge well, so absorptive capacity is high and only normal collection refresh risk argues for removal.

The hand-knotted wool-silk carpet matches the firm's premium craftsmanship and materials positioning, but its more niche and costly market makes pruning somewhat more likely than for broader-volume items.

This low-pile decorative carpet is strongly related to the firm's established offer, so the firm can evaluate demand and refine the product, though overlap with other rug launches raises some rationalization risk.

A corner bench builds directly on the firm's core furniture capabilities in design, customization and project use, making it the kind of adjacent product the firm is well placed to improve and retain.
The low-pile carpet is close to existing competencies and the growing interiors market supports keeping it, but multiple similar carpet introductions increase the chance of assortment consolidation.
A swivel shell chair is highly aligned with the firm's established seating and workplace expertise, so the firm has strong absorptive capacity to learn from early sales and continue developing it.
